Subject: Performance MAP: throughput validation, TTFT & unit-econ playbook

Hi Claire,

Following our sync last week Im capturing a short Mutual Action Plan (MAP) focused specifically on the throughput/latency acceptance criteria and the evaluation plan we discussed. Goal: validate production-grade throughput and unit economics for your real workload so you can finalize the PO by end of November.

High-level asks from LedgerOne: run the workload tests below against our hosted endpoint (or Dedicated if you prefer) and share the raw CSV + a short summary. Well slot analysis and a canary week based on results.

Target acceptance criteria (what wed like to validate):
- Sustained QPS: >= 250 RPS with 95th pct latency (TTFT+streaming) < 140ms
- Avg request tokens: 420 (your sample) -> tokens/sec target ~ 105k
- Concurrent inflight requests: peak concurrency 40 (spike tests to 80)
- Time-to-first-token (TTFT): warm < 60ms, cold < 120ms
- Resilience: graceful degradation to model variant within 2s of failure

Deliverables from LedgerOne test run:
1) CSV timeseries (1s granularity) with RPS, tokens/sec, TTFT (cold/warm), CPU/GPU util.
2) Short PDF with top-line numbers and any anomalies.
3) Updated MAP action items sheet (I attached our template).

Proposed schedule:
- 11/07: LedgerOne runs tests and drops CSV + PDF into the Drive
- 11/10: Redwood analysis call (30m) to review raw metrics and unit-econ light model
- 11/17–11/30: 2-week canary (if acceptance looks good)

If you'd prefer we can run the tests from our side using a replay of your production traces (wed need a sanitized trace export). Let me know which path you want and Ill send a short pre-run checklist.

Attachments: map-action-items-20251102.xlsx (MAP template)

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

- Peak sustained window: 240 RPS for ~10 min (after ramp)

Were available for a review call Tues 11/13 or Wed 11/14.

Neha / Rishi — forwarding LedgerOnes results. Key takeaways below and a quick unit-econ sketch to prep for our review call tomorrow.

Raw numbers (steady):
- Sustained RPS: 212
- Burst observed: 240 for short window
- Avg tokens/request: 412 -> tokens/sec = 212 * 412 = ~87,344
- Warm TTFT: median 42ms, 95th ~110ms
- Cold TTFT median 95ms
- Concurrency observed steady ~34, spikes to 70 caused errors

Interpretation / ask:
1) With the current runtime profile theyre ~15% shy of the 250 RPS goal. We need to know whether a config tweak (profiling batch window, pinning model quantization, or changing kernel flags) can close that gap, or whether the Dedicated pool bump is required.
2) Error behavior at 68+ concurrency suggests queue throttling; we should validate our circuit-breaker and fallback paths.

Quick unit-econ sketch (ballpark):
- Using their steady tokens/sec (~87.3k) -> tokens/hr = 87,344 * 3600 = ~314.4M tokens/hr
- If our marginal infra cost to serve is $0.75 per 1M tokens (internal blended number for this config), hourly cost = 314.4 * $0.75 = $235.8/hr
- For a 30-day sustained profile: $235.8 * 24 * 30 = ~$170,000/month (this is purely infra serving cost; excludes infra management and support fees)
- If we hit their target 250 RPS -> tokens/sec ~103k -> hourly cost delta ~ +$38/hr; so moving to 250 RPS is a modest incremental infra delta vs the overall sustained spend, but it affects reservation sizing.

Proposed next steps for call:
- Neha: propose 2 config experiments (batching profile and kernel config) we can run during a 2-hour window; expected lift: 5–12%
- Rishi: validate our fallback policy to make sure if concurrency>64 we auto-failover to smaller model variant without 5xxs
- Jordan: ask LedgerOne if theyd accept a 7-day canary to measure production traces with real client behavior

Ill run the math live on the call. Marcus, any objections to offering a 7-day complimentary canary credit (small infra credit) to accelerate close?

Regards,
Jordan
